WORRY GUIDE — WORK

When you're torn about starting a side job

You want another source of income, and you'd like to try something different from your main job. But you can't quite get started, because you worry whether your time and energy will hold out, and whether it will affect your main job. Being torn over a side job is a question of how to balance a new possibility against your life as it is now. On this page, we'll look at ways to sort things out when you're torn about starting a side job, and tarot cards that reflect those angles.

POINT 01

What's making this hard

Much of the indecision over a side job is a standoff between the feeling of "I want to try it" and the anxiety of "can I really keep it up?" You're already tired from your main job — can you really spend even more time? Will it go against company rules, and what will people think? Not knowing what to start with, you can also end up spending all your time just gathering information. Wariness of deals that sound too good, and the fear that you might start and earn nothing, also drag the indecision out. Start by putting into words what you want to get from a side job — income, skills, or a sense of fulfillment.

POINT 02

How to sort it out

What helps you sort things out is the idea of "starting small, and finding a form you can keep up." Rather than aiming for a large income from the start, beginning with something you can do in a few hours a week lets you move forward while checking the effect on your main job and your life. Before you start, it will reassure you to check whether your work rules allow side jobs, and to look into how taxes such as the final tax return are handled. The experience you've built up in your current job or hobbies may also be of use to someone just as it is. As well as learning something entirely new, consider the path of making use of abilities you already have.

POINT 03

How to read the cards

When you're torn over a side job, cards that stand for "steady accumulation," "balancing two things," "beginnings," "outlook," "cooperation," and "overlooking something" can offer clues.

The Eight of Pentacles shows someone carefully building up their work piece by piece, honing their craft.

The Two of Pentacles points to the sense of balance in skillfully keeping two things going at once,

and The Magician points to the will to start something with the abilities in your hands.

The Three of Wands stands for the viewpoint of looking out over what lies beyond,

the Three of Pentacles stands for the power to give something shape by working with others,

and the Four of Cups stands for a state in which you haven't noticed an opportunity being offered to you. Check whether what you need right now is preparation or action.

POINT 04

Questions to ask yourself

Try answering the following questions. How many hours a week do you have available for a side job? Even if you use that time, can you protect your sleep and your time with family? Besides money, what do you want to gain through a side job? In your current job or hobbies, is there anything someone has ever asked you to do for them? If you kept it up for six months and saw no results, how would you judge the situation? Is the reason you're putting off starting a lack of preparation, or anxiety? The more concrete your answers, the more clearly you'll see a way of starting that fits you, at a pace you can manage.

CARDS

Cards connected to this decision

  • Eight of Pentacles

    A card for the stance of building up your work one piece at a time and honing your craft.

  • Two of Pentacles

    The sense of keeping two things — your main job and your side job — in balance as you run them.

  • The Magician

    The will to start something using the abilities and experience in your hands.

  • Three of Wands

    The viewpoint of looking out over the possibilities that spread beyond the step you're taking now.

  • Three of Pentacles

    It stands for the power to work with others, give your skills shape, and be recognized for them.

  • Four of Cups

    It asks whether you're overlooking an opportunity being offered right in front of you.

Start a side job, or wait for now? Why not sort out the time you have and the wish to try it?
